newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bunds charge ahead, set to tackle 101.19.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bunds charge ahead, set to tackle 101.19.

text.p: June Bund futures on LIFFE will push ahead to test resistance at 101.19 on Thursday after a robust opening which left shorts on the hop, analysts said.
A late rally in U.S. T-bonds on Thursday, which helped to erase a large chunk of losses in the pit session, continued overnight, giving Bunds an early morning boost, they said.
"It's the U.S. really that's created it," said Norman Beauchamp, head of derivatives at Cooperative Bank in London.
"The markets have been oversold for quite a long time. If we do come back a little, we'll probably look for it to squeeze a little bit higher," he said.
Bunds were quoted at 100.96 at 0653 GMT, up 33 basis points from Thursday's close but off their 101.07 high hit just after the opening.

Beachamp said the market would initially target 101.19, the low on March 14. Beyond there, resistance came in at 101.61, the high on March 17 just before the market dropped sharply to a 100.15 low and ultimately extended the bear move to a 99.05 trough.
"We're now into that area of that whole day," he said.
Analysts at a European bank in London said the main feature on the Bunds' chart was the reverse head and shoulders pattern.
They said in a research note the next goal would be 101.12,13 but over time, the base formed can support a run to the 102.00 area.
Beauchamp said any pullback this session would be well supported at 100.83, Wednesday's mode area -- the area where most volume occured.
Below there, the value area on Wednesay at 100.70 would act as support. The value area is where 70 percent of the mode area takes place, Beauchamp said.
The analysts at the European bank said the market would still be bullish if support at 100.50 held.
They said a drop to the mid 100.30s would be a chance to buy on weakness.
June Euromarks were quoted at 96.76, up 0.01 on the day.
